comment: Legacy-only patch sites, appended by gen_site_table.py after the reverse-engineered table's rows (so the existing row numbers never move). Same fields as that table; every expected byte string is checked against the pinned exe like the others.

Name text lookup char* 0x3214B0(int ref): ref = sub<<11 | index into section 61 ([0x2EBF170]); bounds-checked, returns 0 when out of range. Pure read; safe from the game thread.
Per-character availability int 0x3064F0(u8 member, u16 action, int): 1 = owned (or in a guest fixed list) and licensed. Pure read.
Wait engine call target: acquire pause reason 0x226be0(reason, 0, 0, 0, [rsp+0x20]=-1, [rsp+0x28]=-1). No refcount: a reason already held returns at once.
Wait engine call target: release pause reason 0x225cd0(reason, -1). For reason 0 in Wait mode it also clears the Wait input lock.
Wait engine call target: pause aggregate 0x226280() (applies the combined reason masks; a no-op unless the dirty byte 0x1fd46d0 is set). Also runs at the end of every frame.
Wait engine call target: clear the reason-0 Wait input lock (bit 1 of [0x1f7ffe0]+0x3a), idempotent. Three siblings differ only in the tail-jump displacement, so that displacement stays literal.
Wait engine: frontend id -> pause reason 0x255290(id). Not called; the engine keeps its own copy of this table, which needs the stock function.

Keep running in background: screen-state ApplyActive 0x7a4150 (slot 9 of every screen state; app thread, once per loop from the screen-manager update, before that loop's field tick). rcx = the current state, dl = its active byte, written to the application's active byte (app+0x27) whose 0 opens the focus pause. With the setting on and the state Window (vtable 0x1cb3f50) or Borderless (0x1cb4000): byte [rcx+0x18] = 1 and dl = 1, then the original. Every other state (exclusive fullscreen, its lose-focus and change states) runs the original untouched.
Gate for FP-01: the application's slot +0x70, the only writer of its active byte (byte [rcx+0x27] = dl). If another mod rewrote it, FP-01 is skipped.

Keep running in background, DirectInput pads: 0x7a1a50 (tick thread) after a failed Poll and the first Acquire (the device is not acquired while another window has the foreground). Stock exits past the finalizer and the pad keeps its last state. Setting on and the window not foreground: the neutral block into +0x414..+0x44e, then 0x7a1c9f (mov rcx,rbx; call the finalizer). Anchored here rather than at 0x7a1aa1: a coincidental disp32 elsewhere equals the RVA of 0x7a1aa2.

Keep running in background, DirectInput mouse: 0x7a1790 (tick thread) right after GetDeviceState failed. Stock exits past the finalizer and the buttons +0x1f4..+0x1f6 keep their last level. Setting on and the window not foreground: zero +0x1e8..+0x1f6, then 0x7a1a1e (mov rcx,rbx; call the finalizer). rsi was not saved on this path, so resuming after its restore is correct.
Report only: field input 0x253c70 calls the focus-pause opener 0x228380 here every field tick (its only caller). Another mod's auto-pause switch rewrites this call; FP-01 stays compatible with it.

Report only: the Window screen state's update polls GetForegroundWindow and clears its active byte while the window is not foreground, whatever WM_ACTIVATE delivered (why rewriting the focus event alone cannot keep windowed mode running; FP-01 acts after this poll).

HUD frame hook (H0): the combat-log manager's draw message (msg 4 of handler 0x2be4f0) calls the log draw 0x2bf230(rcx = log manager, rdx = the window's draw context [mgr+0x38]) here, once per frame while the field/battle HUD tree is drawn (window draw 0x245e60 sends msg 3/4/5 only while the window and its ancestors are visible, (flags & 0x405) == 5). Game thread, inside the 2D UI pass. The callee runs first (CALL_AROUND), then the after-handler replays the co-op canvas with the game's own text and sprite functions on a private copy of that context. Vision's No Combat Log NOPs this call: then the row is not stock and stays unhooked (fail-safe: nothing is drawn).
Gate for HD-01: the log draw 0x2bf230 (callee of the frame hook; the native text-draw reference the canvas is held to). If another mod rewrote it, HD-01 is skipped.

signature.pattern: 66 41 0f 6e d0 66 0f 6e ca 0f 5b d2 0f 5b c9 e9 ?? ?? ?? ?? cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc cc 66

sites.purpose: Gate for HD-01: the native text draw 0x2d8650(ctx, int x, int y, params) (int to float, then 0x2d8690). The canvas calls it for every text command. If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.
Gate for HD-01: the text parameter block init 0x2b3400(block 0xd0, string, font) the canvas calls before each text draw, as the log draw does. If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.
Gate for HD-01: the sprite batch begin 0x2d9c40(batch, ctx, 1) of the MRP node draw 0x2435c0, which the canvas uses for sprite commands. If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.
Gate for HD-01: the batched sprite draw 0x2d9380(batch, ctx, texture entry, colours[4], &uvwh, x, y, w, h, 0) of the MRP node draw. If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.
Gate for HD-01: the sprite batch end 0x2d9b00(batch, ctx). If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.
Gate for HD-01: the list selection bar 0x242c90(ctx, x, y, w, h, &rgba) (battle_4_c cap and stretch tinted by the RGBA), the canvas bar. If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.

Gate for HD-01: the texture registry lookup by name 0x24a5a0 (64 entries of 0x48 at 0x208f580, +0x38 bit 0x20 loaded, +0x20 the TIM2 picture header whose eXt block holds the sprite tables). If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.

Native TARGET INFO open: 0x2be1a0 calls the window's set routine 0x2be300(rcx = owner, UI + 0x8fa0 + 0xac0; edx = mode; r8d = id; r9d = handle) here, its only caller; 0x2be1a0 returns before this call when r8d == 0 and r9d < 0, so every call here is an open or update. While the co-op Target Info is live the handler sets r8d = 0 and r9d = -1, the set routine's own close request: no window is created (an open one closes through 0x2bea40) and the resets an open runs (0x290990, 0x35c070, 0x3c53e0) still run. Owner +0x578/+0x57e are read only by 0x2be290, 0x2be300 and the creator 0x2c0f30. Otherwise stock (RUN_ORIGINAL), so the native window and Legacy's target_info_scale.lua return with the element or RENDER off. Game thread.

Party row HP colour (low-HP glow): the party row update 0x29a0a0 calls the HP digits function 0x297d10(rcx = row window, edx = HP shown, r8d = status) here, with rbx = the party-HUD record (+0x24 maximum HP); game thread, once per row update. 0x297d10 returns early while edx == row+0xe0 (the HP cache, written by the caller after the call) and row+0x108 is null. For a low-HP row the handler sets row+0xe0 to -1 around the call (CALL_AROUND; the after-handler puts the cache back, so the HP gauge update 0x297e10 that follows sees it unchanged) so the digits are set again this frame, and arms the glow colour for HD-03. A row it coloured that is no longer low is forced once more with the native colour. Optional: if another mod rewrote the call, the row is skipped.

Party row HP colour (low-HP glow): the `call 0x29f6e0` after `mov rcx, rsi` in 0x297d10 (the call alone: a .rdata dword equals the mov's interior), the digit setter 0x29f6e0(rcx = first digit node, edx = digits, r8d = 0, r9d = RGBA, [rsp+0x20] = HP) with rdi = the row window. When HD-02 armed the glow for this row, r9d becomes the glow colour (the game's own colour argument; the digits' vertex colours are written by the game). Otherwise stock. Optional: if another mod rewrote the call, the row is skipped.
Gate for HD-02: the HP digits function 0x297d10 (callee of HD-02): rdi = row, the early exit on edx == row+0xe0 with row+0x108 null. If it is not stock, HD-02 is skipped.
Gate for HD-03: the digit setter 0x29f6e0(first node, digits, flags, RGBA, value) whose colour argument HD-03 replaces. If it is not stock, HD-03 is skipped.

Gate for HD-02: the arguments of the HP digits call in 0x29a0a0 (r8d = [rbx+0x44] status of the party-HUD record rbx, edx = r15d HP shown, rcx = rbp row window). If they are not stock, HD-02 is skipped.

Seat diamonds: the world-marker dispatcher 0x28eab0 calls the overhead pass 0x2c62b0(rcx = overhead manager, rdx = list A, r8 = list B, r9 = the frame's object pool of 128 x 0x100, [rsp+0x20] = list D) here, its only caller, once per frame. While a seat diamond is visible the handler runs the pass (CALL_AROUND) and the after-handler appends a gem and a numeral per visible seat to list B the way the leader marker 0x2c8920 does: 0x3f0040(pool) (null when the pool is full: emission stops), the overhead record's anchor (+0x00, the record found by handle at +0x10), 0x3f12e0(obj, partytop_4_c, sheet, cell), colour/alpha/quad, 0x3f1290(list B, obj). The pool is reset every frame, so nothing outlives its frame. Otherwise stock (RUN_ORIGINAL). Game thread. Optional: if another mod rewrote the call, no diamonds.

Cleave gate on the stock target list: the list owner 0x2778c0 calls 0x27dc10(ecx = caster, edx = highlighted target, r8w = owner +0xdc action, r9d = row flags & 2) here, its only caller, on a target-list hover; 0x27dc10 releases the other area rings (0x290cd0), asks 0x31ab80 for the action's area and makes a ring (0x28ea20) for kind 1 with r9d clear. For Attack (150), which Legacy's Attack Area Experiment turns into a radius-4 circle for every weapon, the handler sets r9d = 2, the native no-ring flag: the other rings are still released, none is made. Every other action is stock. Game thread. Optional: if another mod rewrote the call, the stock rings stay.

Battle log feed: entry of the battle message emitter 0x46ab10(rcx = producer context, edx = message id, r8 = the 0x30-byte argument block: +0x00/+0x08 battle records of actors A/B, +0x10..+0x28 values, +0x28 the action id its first test bounds below 0x1ff), before its filters, the dedupe ring 0x2ebb560 and the formatter 0x5369c0 (102 templates, no damage numbers). The handler copies edx, rcx and the block into a bounded ring through the fault-safe probe and returns RUN_ORIGINAL: no register, flag or game byte changes, no game call. Any thread that emits a message. Optional: if another mod hooked the entry, the battle log builds its lines from HP and status diffs alone.

Battle log per-hit bracket: entry of the hit function 0x307300(cx = action, rdx = caster actor, r8 = target actor, r9 = hit slot, two stack arguments), called once per target hit from 0x319362. The handler copies the action and both handles ([actor+8], fault-safe) into the battle log ring, opens this thread's bracket (serial, thread id, time) and returns RUN_ORIGINAL: no register, flag or game byte changes, no game call. Optional: if another mod hooked the entry, amounts are not pinned to their hit and the log keeps HP diffs.

Battle log per-hit outcome: 0x307601 in 0x307300 (mov r8, r13; mov rdx, rbx), after the formula on both the native and the Forge path, before the outcome switch: rdi = caster actor, rbx = target actor, r15w = action, r14 = hit slot (+8 the outcome byte: hit, parry, evade, shield, miss, immune, reflected, skipped), r13 = the action row (+0x13 element), al = crit | combo << 1 | counter << 2 | knockback << 3. The handler copies them, the records ([actor+0x698]), the target's affinities (+0x40..+0x43) and the caster's weapon id (+0x50) through the fault-safe probe and returns RUN_ORIGINAL. The call at 0x30760a, which another mod rewrites, stays outside the window. Optional: without it the log has no outcome tags.

Battle log exact numbers: entry of the number pop-up 0x3283d0(rcx = actor, edx = signed amount, r8b = heal, r9b = 1 for MP), called by the native HP and MP appliers inside 0x307300 and by the Forge from its Lua thread. The handler copies the amount only when the calling thread has the open bracket (HR-01 .. HR-05); every other call is counted, not copied. RUN_ORIGINAL always. Optional: without it, amounts come from diffs.

Battle log per-hit bracket: the common exit of 0x307300 (mov rcx, [rbp+0xa0], before the stack check and the epilogue), which every path reaches, the Forge's jump included. The handler closes this thread's bracket and copies its serial; it reads no register. RUN_ORIGINAL always. Optional, with HR-01.

Battle log kill reward: entry of the EXP and LP pop-up 0x28fb80(ecx = victim handle, edx = EXP, r8d = LP), its only caller the kill reward 0x312280 (0x312518), after the chain update and the EXP and LP credit. The handler copies the three registers into the ring (any thread: the Forge runs 0x312280 from its Lua thread) and returns RUN_ORIGINAL. Optional: without it the kill line has no EXP or LP.

Gate for HR-02: the flag stores before it (test al, n; or [r14+8], flag), where both the native and the Forge path arrive with the flag nibble in eax: eax is only tested up to HR-02, r14 is the hit slot, rdi the caster. If another mod rewrote them, HR-02 is skipped.

Gate for HR-02: the outcome switch after the call at 0x30760a (movzx eax, byte [r14+8]; cmp eax, 0xa; ja): the slot byte HR-02 copies is the one the game switches on. If it is not stock, HR-02 is skipped.

sites.purpose: Gate for HR-01: the only call of 0x307300 at 0x319362 with its first two arguments (rdx = the caster, ecx = the action). If another mod rewrote the call or them, HR-01 is skipped.
Gate for HR-01: the same call's other arguments (r8 = the target, r9 = the hit slot, the flag at [rsp+0x28]). If another mod rewrote them, HR-01 is skipped.

Gate for HR-03: the number pop-up's prologue after HR-03 (rbx = the actor, edi = heal * 2 | MP, esi = the amount): the registers HR-03 copies mean what it says. If they are not stock, HR-03 is skipped.
Gate for HR-05: the rest of the common exit of 0x307300 up to the stack release (xor rcx, rsp; the stack check; add rsp, 0x1c8). If it is not stock, HR-05 is skipped.

Gate for KR-01: the kill reward's call of the pop-up (ecx = [r14+8] the victim handle, r8d = LP, edx = EXP or 0 in the no-EXP mode), up to the call's end; the patch another mod writes at 0x312524 starts after it. If it is not stock, KR-01 is skipped.

Target Info give-back check: the TARGET INFO owner tick 0x2be290 (owner = UI + 0x9a60): owner +0x57e bit 0 = pending create, built through 0x2bea40 and the creator 0x2c0f30; owner +0x570 = the current window; window +0x280 bit 0 closing, bit 2 = invalid, closed here. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

sites.purpose: Target Info give-back check: the HUD window update 0x2be490 (message 2) ends by calling the owner tick 0x2be290 with rcx = HUD + 0xac0, so a pending create is consumed on the next HUD update. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the creator 0x2c0f30 reads the id from owner +0x578 and the form from owner +0x57e bit 2. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the window update 0x2bfd20 returns at once when window +0x280 bit 2 (invalid) is set. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the window update 0x2bfd20 resolves window +0x288 and sets window +0x280 bit 2 when the handle no longer resolves. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the handle resolver 0x3588b0 decodes index bits 0..15, registry bits 16..19 and generation bits 20..30, registries below 5. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the field target mode 0x3c9420 requests the TARGET INFO with mode 6 and the id, then compares it with the target-mode window [0x2b47730] +0xc4. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the window core focus change 0x244830 clears window +0x40 bit 0x10 (input focus) on the window losing it. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Target Info give-back check: the TARGET INFO request entry 0x28fe40 reads the UI manager [0x209be80] and uses HUD = UI + 0x8fa0. Information for the patch layer; the native Target Info give-back acts only while every TI-V row is stock.

Guests' interaction prompt: the overhead pass 0x2c62b0 calls the prompt drawer 0x2c7f90(rcx = overhead manager, rdx = P1's prompt widget at manager +0x1b80, r8 = list B, r9 = the frame's object pool, [rsp+0x20] = list D) here, its only caller, once per frame. While a guest's private interaction pass found something (or a guest marker is fading out) the handler runs the drawer (CALL_AROUND) and the after-handler appends the same native marker once per such guest to list B: 0x3f0040(pool) (null when the pool is full: emission stops), the battle_4_p frame [sheet first + [0x916f00 + level - 1]], the level's key table (0x916e10 / 0x916e40) and the lift curve through 0x2c6dc0, 0x2c69a0(the guest's overhead record, obj, frame, alpha, 0x80808080, texture), 0x2708b0 scale, the drawer's offsets, 0x3f1290(list B, obj). The pool is reset every frame and every time and level is the handler's own: nothing of the game's state is written. Otherwise stock (RUN_ORIGINAL). Game thread. Optional: if another mod rewrote the call, guests get no marker.

Gate for HD-01: the scissor setter 0x2d8530(context): context+0x5c bit 0x20000 set = clip to the context's rect at +0x48, clear = no clip (0x249fd0 -> 0x184460). The window draw 0x245e60 calls it before a window's messages, so a canvas drawn inside the log manager's draw is clipped to the log window unless the replay lifts the clip and puts it back. If it is not stock, HD-01 is skipped.

Overlay frame hook: the render-command dispatcher 0x607410 (switch on the command id, 0x28 cases) calls the present wrapper 0x6234a0(rcx = renderer) here, its only caller, once per presented frame, on the render-ring consumer thread that owns the immediate context. The handler reads the game's device, immediate context and swap chain at renderer +0x108/+0x110/+0x118, draws the co-op overlay into the back buffer with its own D3D11 objects (every pipeline state it touches saved and restored), then runs the wrapper (RUN_ORIGINAL), which flushes and presents. Optional: if another mod rewrote the call, there is no overlay and the guests' menus stay idle (no presenter).
Gate for OV-01: the present wrapper 0x6234a0 takes the renderer in rcx and flushes its immediate context at +0x110 (vtable +0x378, Flush) first. If it is not stock, OV-01 is skipped.
Gate for OV-01: inside the present wrapper, IDXGISwapChain::Present (vtable +0x40) on the swap chain at renderer +0x118. If it is not stock, OV-01 is skipped.

Gate for OV-01: the arguments of the renderer's D3D11CreateDeviceAndSwapChain call at 0x625a64: ppSwapChain = renderer +0x118, ppDevice = renderer +0x108, ppImmediateContext = renderer +0x110, SDK version 7, desc Windowed and ALLOW_MODE_SWITCH. If it is not stock, OV-01 is skipped (the offsets the handler reads are no longer proven).

Vanilla HUD hide check: the window draw 0x245e60 draws a window and its subtree only while (flags & 0x405) == 5 (bit 0 drawn, bit 2 updated, bit 10 destroyed). Information for the patch layer; the overlay hides the party list, the help line, Target Info and the second log window by bit 0 only while every HH-V row is stock.
Vanilla HUD hide check: the party panel getter returns [[0x209be80] + 0x10f78].
Vanilla HUD hide check: the party panel is created with handler 0x29be50.
Vanilla HUD hide check: the two help-line slots are embedded at HUD + 0xc0 and + 0x5c0 (layout group 7).
Vanilla HUD hide check: a help-line slot is created with handler 0x2bf690.
Vanilla HUD hide check: the per-frame tree update sends message 2 without testing bit 0, so a hidden window keeps its values current.
Vanilla HUD hide check: the second combat-log window (handler 0x2c0b40) is stored at HUD + 0x1078 by the log setup (which also sets bit 2 of the first log window's +0xec).

Party HUD read check: the party-HUD record filler copies current MP (s16 battle record +0x4c) and MP max (s16 +0x28). Information for the patch layer; the overlay's party list reads MP max only while PH-V1 is stock.
Party HUD read check: the filler copies the action charge, current (actor +0x768) and required (+0x76c), the action gauge's source. The overlay reads the gauge only while PH-V2..PH-V4 are stock.
Party HUD read check: the gauge charges while the action (actor +0x714) is a battle action and the state (actor +0x6b4) is at least 3.
Party HUD read check: the gauge is full while the state (actor +0x6b4) is at least 9 (executing).
